title: Rate limiting for a node:http server
when: A Node API or form endpoint needs protection from floods, brute force logins, or a client calling too often.
prompt:
Goal: A per client limiter that answers 429 with Retry-After, uses little memory and is tunable per route.
Steps:
1. Key by req.socket.remoteAddress; read X-Forwarded-For only when configured to run behind a known proxy.
2. Token bucket per key: capacity 20, refill 10 per second; keep { tokens, updated } in a Map and refill from elapsed time on each request.
3. Under one token: 429 with retry-after seconds and JSON { error: "rate_limited" }; otherwise take a token and continue.
4. Stricter buckets for sensitive routes (login: 5 per minute per address and per username); none for static files.
5. Send RateLimit-Limit and RateLimit-Remaining headers.
6. Sweep idle keys every minute with an unref timer and cap the Map size; unknown routes still answer 404.
Quality bar:
- Normal use never hits the limit.
- The limiter runs before body parsing, so floods are cheap to reject.
- Limits live in config.
Pitfalls:
- Trusting X-Forwarded-For from anyone, letting clients pick their key.
- Fixed windows that allow double bursts at the edge.
- A Map that never forgets keys.
Verify:
- [ ] 429 responses carry retry-after.
- [ ] Idle entries are swept.
- [ ] Login has its own limit.
- [ ] A 404 fallback remains.
Output: ratelimit.mjs exporting createLimiter(options), called first in the server request handler.

examples.input: bloquear quem tenta muitas senhas no login
examples.output: token bucket per IP and per username on POST /login, 429 with retry-after, idle sweep
